title: Claude Cowork
content:
## What Is Cowork?

**Cowork** is Anthropic's agentic assistant for non-technical, general-computing work — effectively a Claude Code-like experience for the rest of the office, not just developers. It launched in January 2026, built on the same underlying agent foundations as Claude Code but packaged for people who never touch a terminal: give Claude access to a folder on your computer, describe a task in plain language, and Cowork reads, edits, and organizes files on your behalf.

---

## Timeline

| Date | Milestone |
|---|---|
| January 2026 | Initial launch, baked into the macOS Claude desktop app |
| February 2026 | Tool integrations: Google Drive, Gmail, DocuSign, FactSet |
| March 2026 | **Projects** feature — keeps files, instructions, and task context organized in one workspace |
| April 2026 | Enterprise features: role-based access control, group management via SCIM/identity providers; Zoom MCP connector for meeting summaries, action items, and transcripts |
| July 2026 | Expanded to **web and mobile**, with sessions able to run remotely; taken out of preview into general enterprise availability |
| August 2026 | Full desktop/web/mobile parity; sessions save state to the user's Claude account and sync across devices |

---

## How It Differs from Claude Code

Both products share an agentic core — reasoning, tool use, file access, multi-step task execution — but target different users and surfaces:

- **Claude Code** is a CLI/IDE-first tool aimed at software engineers working in a codebase with git, tests, and shell commands.
- **Cowork** is aimed at general office workers: it operates on documents, spreadsheets, email, and business tools rather than source code, and is designed to need no command-line familiarity at all.

---

## Background and Cross-Device Sessions (2026)

As of the July 2026 mobile/web expansion, Cowork sessions run in the cloud by default rather than being tied to a single desktop instance. This gives it the same core benefits Claude Code gets from its own cloud/remote sessions:

- **Cross-device continuity** — start a task on desktop, check progress from a phone
- **Background execution** — work continues after closing the laptop
- **Scheduled tasks** — recurring Cowork tasks now run server-side rather than requiring the desktop app to stay open

---

## Enterprise Adoption

Anthropic moved Cowork out of preview and into general enterprise availability alongside the mobile/web launch. Enterprise-focused capabilities include:

- **Role-based access control**, with group management either manual or via identity-provider integration (cross-domain identity management / SCIM-style provisioning)
- **MCP connectors** to business tools (Zoom, Google Drive, Gmail, DocuSign, FactSet) so Cowork can pull in meeting transcripts, documents, and records directly
- **Inference hooks** (beta, shared with Claude Code and Chat) — real-time DLP enforcement that inspects prompts and tool calls before they reach the model, aimed at compliance teams

---

## Why It Matters

Cowork represents Anthropic extending the "agent that acts in your files" pattern proven by Claude Code to a much larger, non-technical audience, and doing so with the same cloud-session infrastructure (background execution, cross-device sync, scheduled server-side tasks) that Claude Code adopted for its own remote sessions. It's a useful comparison point for anyone building agentic products: the same session-continuity and background-task patterns are becoming standard across Anthropic's agent surfaces, not just the developer-focused ones.
